title: Epping Forest folklore and history-linked locations
notes: Coordinates are WGS84 decimal latitude/longitude.
Some entries are folklore or urban legend rather than verified history. Confidence indicates confidence in the location/story link, not that the story is historically true.
Where a source gives only a road, grid square, or nearby landmark, coordinates are marked approximate.
Some coordinates are deliberately rough location anchors for folklore where the exact place is disputed, lost, or only described orally.
Do not treat low-confidence entries as verified history; they are included because they are recurring local legends or ghost-story motifs linked to Epping Forest.
v4 adds additional royal-history and crime-history records; several modern-crime coordinates are rough locality anchors to avoid implying exact private or sensitive sites.
Bomb-site coordinates are approximate unless marked otherwise; several entries represent general habitat or wartime-use areas rather than exact impact points.
Version 7 adds extra location-tied heritage stories, including literary traditions, public-access history, ancient-tree landscapes, science landmarks and modern filming associations.
Version 8 adds a film and television layer. Specific named locations are preferred; generic Forest credits are marked with very approximate coordinates.
Version 9 adds additional film and TV references requested by the user. Several are deliberately marked general_forest or general_area because public sources do not identify exact filming pins.

Version 10 adds notable-person and celebrity associations. Private residences are intentionally represented only at town, estate, pub, plaque or public-institution level; exact private home coordinates are not included.
Version 11 adds a dedicated blue plaque / heritage plaque category.
Loughton and Epping plaques are based on council-published lists. Coordinates are approximate from public addresses and should be geocoded for exact walking navigation.

Nearby towns checked include Loughton, Epping, Buckhurst Hill and Waltham Forest areas such as Chingford, Woodford, Wanstead, Leytonstone and Highams Park. Broader Waltham Forest and Buckhurst Hill coverage is marked as non-exhaustive unless a specific plaque list was available.
Version 12 expands the research scope beyond Epping and Loughton to cover Forest-edge towns, Epping Forest District towns/villages, and the London-side Forest settlements.
Future research passes should run each category across the expanded_search_places list, not just Epping and Loughton.
Public locations are given as precisely as practical. Rough-area entries include location_precision and notes explaining the uncertainty.
Version 13 adds broad interesting layers: ancient trees, hidden infrastructure, common rights, haunted roads, counterculture, conservation/legal history and research-source records.
Entries marked dataset_layer, route, forest_wide or multiple_public_sites_need_geocoding should be treated as themes or imports to refine later, not exact walking pins.
Precise public sites are preferred where available; folklore and private/uncertain claims are marked approximate or rough_area.
Version 14 adds external_links to each location, converting raw sources into labelled links suitable for an app UI.
Umbrella external links are included for broader research categories such as official Forest history, filming, ancient trees, blue plaques and folklore.
Links are categorised by source type; source quality still varies, so folklore/local-story sources should be displayed differently from official or council sources.
